events.title: Cabral Sights the Coast of Brazil
events.description: Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral, leading a large fleet bound for India, sighted land on the coast of what is now Brazil. He was the first European to do so, and he claimed the territory for Portugal.
events.significance: The landfall began Portugal's colonization of Brazil. Brazil went on to become the largest Portuguese-speaking nation in the world.

events.title: Birth of Immanuel Kant
events.description: The philosopher Immanuel Kant was born in Königsberg, in Prussia. He spent almost his entire life in the city and became one of the most influential thinkers of the Enlightenment.
events.significance: Kant's work on knowledge, ethics and reason, especially his Critique of Pure Reason, still shapes philosophy, science and political thought today.

events.title: "In God We Trust" Authorized for U.S. Coins
events.description: During the Civil War, the U.S. Congress passed the Coinage Act of 1864. It allowed the motto "In God We Trust" to appear on American coins, and the two-cent piece was the first to carry it.
events.significance: The motto became a lasting feature of U.S. currency. In 1956 it was officially adopted as the national motto.

events.title: The First Earth Day
events.description: Millions of Americans took part in rallies, teach-ins and demonstrations for a healthier environment. The events were held at campuses, schools and in communities across the country.
events.significance: Earth Day helped drive the creation of major environmental laws and agencies in the United States. It has since grown into a worldwide annual observance.
